description:
Adds the AVX2 backend of the lane kernel bundle in `gf2-kernels-simd`, bit-identical to the portable backend, behind runtime detection and explicit safety contracts.

## Background

An inter-frame decoder places the same message position of eight independent frames in the eight f32 lanes of one AVX2 register. A lane is a frame, so no reduction inside a check and no accumulation inside a variable is reassociated, and each frame's result equals the single-frame decoder's bit for bit. `gf2-kernels-simd` holds the lane kernel bundle, its portable implementation and the behavioural suite a backend runs; it is one of the two crates that may contain `unsafe`. The register-width forms of the kernel compile at Rust 1.95 and agree with the canonical scalar statements, including on signed zeros and NaN: the record is `dev/bench_results/ed3d490e/intrinsic-feasibility/feasibility.json`, written from the probe crate under `dev/active/ed3d490e-zen3-ldpc-frame-simd/survey/intrinsics-probe/`. The canonical sign is a comparison against zero and the two-minimum fold is a strict comparison, which the vector forms keep by comparing and blending; `docs/reference/ldpc-decoder-numerical-contract.md` states the rules.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: An AVX2 implementation of the lane kernel bundle is published only through a safe detection entry point that returns no bundle on a host without AVX2.
- [hard] REQ-02: The AVX2 bundle passes the kernel behavioural suite with bit patterns identical to the portable bundle, and a test fails if a lane takes the IEEE sign bit of a negative-zero message or lets a NaN magnitude enter a minimum.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each `unsafe` function and block states its safety contract: the target-feature precondition and the slice-length relations its safe entry point checks; an entry point that skips a check is named unchecked and documents its precondition.
- [hard] REQ-04: On a host without AVX2 the AVX2 assertions are reported as not run; they cannot be reported as passed without executing the kernel.
- [hard] REQ-05: The emitted-assembly artefact of the kernel source is regenerated at Rust 1.95 and committed beside it, and shows the check and variable inner loops as packed single-precision instructions without a call or a per-lane scalar path.
- [hard] REQ-06: The crate builds and its tests pass at Rust 1.95.

## Notes

Alignment of the lane type makes each edge one aligned 32-byte load; the kernel takes no dependency on the horizontal `minsum_fn` kernel.
title: Vectorize the lane kernels with AVX2
